question: On which positive edge-weight chamber is Q_anchor=AB the unique rank-four J-invariant Dirichlet-cut minimizer, and is that chamber enforced by the sourced link potential or repeated charges?

y.meaning: squared Dirac-edge norm and Q_anchor boundary cost

action.formula: S_rho(Q)=(1/4)Tr([D,Q]^*[D,Q])=the sum of rho_e over quotient edges crossing Q
action.domain: rho=(x,y,z,u,v,r,s) with every used coordinate strictly positive
action.geometry: the selection regions are open rational polyhedral cones in squared-edge-weight space

H12.compressedForm: y is smaller than the sum of the two smallest members of {x,z,u,v}
H12.unitPoint: strict interior with margin one on every facet

H16.unitPoint: codimension-two boundary intersection y=u=v; AB, DG and FH tie

potentialAndChargeAudit.claim1542StableAllLinkCondition: all six charged VEVs and the neutral coefficient are nonzero; this implies positivity of the seven weights but no ordering among them
potentialAndChargeAudit.generalRenormalizablePotential: contains independent modulus masses and quartics, so its allowed coefficient space does not impose any of the six selection facets
potentialAndChargeAudit.claim1542Witness: all link coefficients and the neutral coefficient equal one
potentialAndChargeAudit.witnessOnH12: strictly inside the H12 selection cone
potentialAndChargeAudit.witnessOnH16: on y=u and y=v, hence not in the unique-selection cone
potentialAndChargeAudit.repeatedChargeFieldIdentificationOnly: a=b and e=f as scalar fields does not imply x=y or v=r because the edge Yukawa maps remain independent
potentialAndChargeAudit.tiedYukawaAddOn: if repeated-charge Yukawas are also tied, then x=y and v=r
potentialAndChargeAudit.tiedYukawaVerdict: the equalities remove four redundant facets on H16 but do not enforce either remaining ordering; the all-one witness saturates both

perturbationAudit.model: independent threshold or one-loop shifts rho_e -> rho_e+delta_e, restricted only by rho_e+delta_e>0
perturbationAudit.exactStabilityRule: replace every rho in the six strict facet inequalities by rho+delta; selection persists exactly while every resulting margin remains positive
perturbationAudit.interiorRobustness: every interior point has a nonzero open neighborhood of perturbations preserving Q_anchor
perturbationAudit.H16UnitPointOtherFacets: the other four facets have unit margin and therefore remain inactive for sufficiently small shifts
perturbationAudit.genericUnitPointBehavior: independent arbitrarily small shifts resolve the AB/DG/FH tie in any of the three directions; AB is not radiatively selected without beta-function ordering

decision.H12RobustSelection: SAT on a nonempty open untuned polyhedral chamber containing the all-link unit vacuum
decision.H16RobustSelection: SAT on a nonempty open untuned polyhedral chamber, but the claim-1542 symmetric vacuum lies on two degeneracy walls
decision.strongestConclusion: Unique anchor selection is structurally stable once the six strict inequalities hold, so it does not require fine tuning; however, neither the stable all-link potential nor repeated-charge identifications force that chamber. Predictive selection on H16 needs a new dynamical ordering or beta-function law, not another equality assumption.

boundary: The chamber calculation treats the seven squared primitive edge norms as scalar positive coordinates. Matrix-valued family Yukawas would replace them by trace norms in the action and can introduce noncommuting spectral data not classified here.
